title: Nut-free coconut-flour pie crust
summary: A nut-free press-in pie shell built on coconut flour, with eggs to bind it because coconut flour soaks up so much liquid.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Grease a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish.
Whisk the coconut flour, erythritol and salt together.
Beat the eggs with the melted butter and vanilla, then stir them into the dry mix to make a soft dough.
Let the dough stand 10 minutes. Coconut flour keeps absorbing liquid, and the dough firms up into something that presses cleanly instead of sticking.
Press the dough evenly over the base and up the sides of the dish, about 5 mm (1/4 in) thick. Wet fingers help if it sticks.
Prick the base all over and bake 12–14 minutes, until firm and just golden at the rim.
Cool before filling. For a filling that bakes in the shell, pre-bake only 8 minutes.

swaps.note: melted; keeps the crust nut-free, unlike many dairy-free butters

dairy_free_notes: Coconut oil makes a firmer, crisper shell when cold and a slightly greasier one when warm; it also deepens the coconut flavour.
tips: Do not add more coconut flour if the dough looks wet at first; give it the full 10 minutes to thicken.
Check the label of any dairy-free butter if you need the crust truly nut-free: many are made with cashew or almond.

origin.history: This is a modern recipe. Coconut flour, the dried and ground pulp left after pressing coconut milk, was taken up widely by gluten-free, paleo and low-carb home bakers in the United States in the 2000s. Press-in shells like this one imitate a traditional pie crust for people who avoid both wheat and nuts.
